messages:
arian: quick idea — add a tiny runtime 'probe' call that routers/control-plane can use to negotiate features with the serving runtime before routing. keeps manifests small and localizes capability checks to the path that needs them.

devon: sketch the surface? how does it fit with the existing model pin + adapter handshake?

arian: minimal. a POST /v1/probe that takes model id + light hints (seq_len, requested features) and returns a compact capability set + recommended fallback and an advisory cost multiplier. response intentionally opaque — no kernel internals. example: 

```http
POST /v1/probe
{
  "model": "redwood-rtx-13b",
  "seq_len": 256,
  "features": ["kv_cache", "streaming", "quant_a8"]
}

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{
  "supports": ["kv_cache", "streaming"],
  "fallbacks": ["redwood-rtx-13b-q4a"],
  "cost_multiplier": "1.12",
  "cap_hash": "sha256:abcd...",
  "ttl_seconds": 60
}
```

mira: curious about security + information leakage — we can't let hosted routers probe a customer's private runtime and learn configs. who is allowed to call this?

arian: yes — call surface is inside our trust boundary. hosted routers call hosted runtimes; for private/VPC/on-prem we expose a local probe endpoint that only the control plane or local router can call (mTLS + attestation). responses should only include boolean flags and stable identifiers (cap_hash) — no perf counters or kernel flags.

samir: cost_multiplier in response worries me. that could be misused for billing surprises.

devon: agree, make it advisory and require attestation. the control plane can sign an attestation token that includes cap_hash + signed_timestamp. billing must use separate pricing contract, but router can prefer cheaper fallback when policy allows.

arian: thinking versioning: /v1/probe and a minimal canonical schema; include cap_hash for caching and signed_attestation for hosted. TTL small (like 30-120s) to allow quick changes but avoid excessive calls.

mira: implementation notes for Private: local control plane writes a small JSON capability file on disk for the runtime, probe reads that; no external network calls. For Dedicated, runtime exposes both probe and a health-ish cap endpoint.

eng-bot: deploy-bot: canary job for probe-endpoint landed on staging.  :rocket:

devon: operational concerns — need to avoid probe storms. router should cache by (model+seq_len_bucket+cap_hash) and backoff on repeated failures. Also make probe idempotent and lightweight.

arian: fallback policy changes: add three-tier fallback semantics — (1) immediate compatible fallback, (2) best-effort fallback with potential cost delta, (3) error/notify. Default is (1) then (2) if policy allows.

samir: sync with billing + quota people before we ship. maybe expose cost_multiplier only in an 'explain' mode not used for real-time quota until billing signoff.

mira: simple security wishlist: mTLS + attestation token for hosted, RBAC for who can call probe in control plane, and scrubbed responses for cross-tenant requests.

arian: agreed. next action: I'll draft a short RFC with schema + attestation flow + TTL rules + router caching algorithm. link when done. :+1:

devon: timeline? can we get a minimal v1 in 2 sprints (runtime + router + minimal CP attestation)?

arian: yep aiming for prototype in staging in sprint 2. I'll ping infra and billing.

samir: thanks — adding a short checklist comment in the RFC for billing/console changes.

mira: :eyes: will review security sections.

arian: closing thread for now, will drop RFC link here when posted.
